newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France back in profit, seeks to privatize.
newsitem.headline: Air France back in profit, seeks to privatize.

text.p: French state airline Air France said Thursday it made a small profit last year, its first since 1989, and the airline's management renewed a plea for privatisation.

The centre-right government has slated the airline for sale to the private sector, but the cloud of a parliamentary election hangs over the plan. Left-wing parties have a chance at gaining power Sunday after winning a first-round vote.
Air France reported a net consolidated profit of 394 million francs ($68.5 million) despite a loss of 250 million francs ($44 million) due to strikes, Managing Director Patrice Durand told reporters.

The result includes profits from subsidiaries like Servair, Air Charter and Jet Tour but not short- and medium-haul airline Air France Europe -- otherwise known as Air Inter -- which was to publish separate results.
Air France had a consolidated loss of 2.264 billion francs ($400.8 million) in the preceding financial year ended March 31, 1996.
Durand said he hoped Air France would be "a bit more than at break-even" at the end of a 1997-98 financial year in which its Air France Europe unit will be merged with the parent company.

The recovery from years of losses in the 1996-97 financial year showed the airline had the potential to catch up with leaders like British Airways and should not miss out on the chance to privatise, he told a news conference.

"We are a public enterprise, but one which lives in a totally competitive world just like goods and services companies. Economic logic weighs heavily in favour of privatisation," Durand told reporters.

The airline said consolidated turnover in the year ended March 31 rose to 46.4 billion francs ($8.2 billion) from 43.23 billion francs ($7.7 billion) a year earlier and that operating profit jumped to 1.14 billion francs ($201.8 million) from 420 million ($74 million) in the 1995-96 financial year.
The airline said turnover in the past financial year rose mainly due to a rise of 2.7 billion francs ($477 million) in passenger and baggage revenues.
